# Data-quality record (auto-generated by `python -m pathsnap.cli explore`)

Partitions analysed: train = 80 trips, student_test = 10 trips. Evaluator-test data is NOT present and was never used.

## Issues, assumptions and decisions

| # | Observation (measured) | Decision / assumption |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sampling is nominally 1 Hz: 96.7% of all steps are exactly 1 s (pooled; per-trip median 99.1%, worst trip 53%); 1260 gaps >5 s and 135 gaps >30 s in total; the two largest gaps are 153064 s in trip 00000090, 52810 s in trip 00000078 (recording paused). | Time-gap features (`dt_prev`, `dt_next`); neighbour/window features ignore neighbours >10 s away; speed uses only valid neighbours. |
| 2 | Missing values: 0 NaN cells; invalid (0,0/out-of-range) coordinates: 0; duplicate timestamps: 0; timestamps going backwards: 0. | No imputation needed for raw files. Rows are kept in time order. |
| 3 | Implausible speeds (>60 m/s) occur in 20 trips (555 steps) - GPS jumps. | Not deleted (the model must cope with noise at test time); jumps are captured by window features. |
| 4 | Coordinates are lon/lat degrees and trips are in many cities (25 UTM zones). | Each trip is projected to the UTM zone of its own centroid; all distances in metres. |
| 5 | Road networks are directed: 92% of arcs have a reverse arc (two-way roads). Both directions of one road lie at the same distance from a GPS point. | Direction features (`heading_diff_deg`, `cos_heading`, `along_advance_m`, `has_reverse`) separate them. |
| 6 | Connectivity: median largest-component share = 98.0% of nodes; 89 of 90 networks have >1 weakly-connected component; isolated nodes total = 0. | Disconnected parts exist; transitions between disconnected arcs are handled by the HMM (Person 3). |
| 7 | Reference route: 14 breaks (end node of arc i != start node of arc i+1) over 90 trips; 10 trips revisit an arc. | Treated as reference, not perfect truth. Breaks are not repaired. |
| 8 | `.route` has far fewer rows than the track (272 route arcs vs 1496 GPS points, medians): it is a list of ARCS, not one label per point. | Point labels are derived by a monotone dynamic-programming alignment (`labels.py`). |
| 9 | Reference route covers only part of the GPS trace in 2 trip(s): 00000033 (route/path = 0.13, 59% of points >50 m from reference), 00000054 (route/path = 0.19, 89% of points >50 m from reference). | Flagged `trip_ok = False`, excluded from training/CV/optimisation (fold = -1); still listed in the inventory. |
| 10 | Points >50 m from the aligned reference arc in otherwise-good trips: 1.27% of points. | `label_valid = False` for these points; not used as training/validation labels (the reference does not cover them). |
| 11 | Candidate radius 75 m gives candidate-miss-rate 0.87% over ALL points of reliable train trips (0.00% over valid-label points, which is ~0 by construction) with 15.8 candidates/point (see radius_study.csv). | Fixed radius 75 m, max 40 nearest candidates. |

## Label definition (important for the viva)

For each GPS point the label arc is the reference-route arc it was aligned to (monotone DP minimising point-to-arc distance, capped at 150 m). A candidate row has `label = 1` iff its arc equals that arc. This is a *derived* label; its limitations are the items 8-10 above.

## Leakage controls

- Feature code (`features.py`) never reads `.route`; `load_trip(with_route=False)` is the inference path.
- Folds are by trip (GroupKFold style), so no trip's points are split across train/validation.
- Only train + student_test were read; no learned preprocessing exists (features are deterministic functions of geometry), so nothing is fitted on test data.
